quests.instruction: Smoke and fumes from heavy traffic can make which kind of problem worse for some people?
quests.hint: It affects how easily you can breathe.
quests.explanation: Exhaust fumes make the air dirtier. This can irritate lungs and make breathing harder, especially for children, older people, and people with asthma.
quests.funFact: Cleaner transport can help the air in cities become healthier.

quests.instruction: Which helps clean the air and gives shade along busy streets?
quests.hint: It has leaves and roots.
quests.explanation: Trees catch dust and some pollution from the air, and they give shade that makes streets cooler.
quests.funFact: Trees along roads can also reduce noise a little.

quests.instruction: When engines burn fuel, they release gases that trap heat around Earth. What does this make the planet?
quests.hint: Think of a blanket wrapped around Earth.
quests.explanation: Some gases trap the sun's heat, like a blanket. More of them in the air makes the world warmer over time.
quests.funFact: Using less fuel, by walking, cycling, and sharing rides, helps reduce these gases.

quests.instruction: Which makes no exhaust smoke and is small enough to carry onto a train?
quests.hint: You power it with your foot.
quests.explanation: A kick scooter uses only your own energy, so it makes no exhaust. Many scooters fold, so they fit on trains and buses.
quests.funFact: Mixing scooters or bikes with trains is a good way to cover the last part of a trip.

quests.instruction: Wind turbines make electricity that can power electric trains. Which natural source is that?
quests.hint: You can feel it on your face.
quests.explanation: Wind is a renewable source, which means it does not run out. Wind turbines turn its movement into electricity.
quests.funFact: Some railways buy electricity from wind farms to power their trains.

quests.instruction: Which of these took millions of years to form and will eventually run out?
quests.hint: It is pumped from deep underground.
quests.explanation: Oil, from which petrol and diesel are made, formed from ancient plants and animals over millions of years. Once it is used up, it cannot be replaced quickly.
quests.funFact: That is why people are looking for renewable energy for transport.

quests.instruction: Four friends who live next door to each other go to the same school. How many cars are needed if they share one?
quests.hint: Share the ride.
quests.explanation: Sharing rides, or carpooling, puts fewer cars on the road. That saves fuel, reduces fumes, and eases traffic.
quests.funFact: Some schools help families find others to share rides with.

quests.instruction: Some people can do their jobs on a computer. Which choice avoids a daily commuting journey altogether?
quests.hint: No travelling needed.
quests.explanation: Working from home means no journey to an office. That saves time and cuts traffic.
quests.funFact: Even working from home a few days a week can make roads quieter.

quests.instruction: A team can meet by video instead of flying 1,000 kilometres. Which tool makes this possible?
quests.hint: It has a screen and a camera.
quests.explanation: Video calls let people meet without long journeys. This saves time, money, and fuel.
quests.funFact: Video calls and online learning became much more common in the last few years.

quests.instruction: A shopper wants food that has travelled the shortest distance. Which source should they choose?
quests.hint: Closer to home means a shorter trip.
quests.explanation: Food that is grown nearby needs a shorter journey to reach you. Less transport can mean less fuel and fresher food.
quests.funFact: Some foods travel thousands of kilometres before reaching shops.

quests.instruction: For moving heavy goods a long way over land, which usually uses less fuel per tonne than a lorry?
quests.hint: Its steel wheels roll with very little friction.
quests.explanation: Steel wheels on steel rails roll easily, so a train can move heavy loads using less fuel than lorries. Planes use much more.
quests.funFact: One freight train can carry as much as many lorries.

quests.instruction: Per box delivered across the ocean, which creates the least pollution?
quests.hint: It carries thousands of boxes at a time.
quests.explanation: A big cargo ship carries so many boxes that each box uses little fuel. Planes burn much more per box.
quests.funFact: Ship engines are being improved to burn cleaner fuels.

quests.instruction: Green bridges built over some roads let which animals cross safely?
quests.hint: Think of forest animals.
quests.explanation: Wildlife bridges and tunnels help animals cross busy roads safely. This protects both animals and drivers.
quests.funFact: Some places even have rope bridges for squirrels and monkeys.

quests.instruction: In some coastal places, which animal crosses the road at night to lay eggs on the beach, so drivers must slow down?
quests.hint: It has a shell.
quests.explanation: Sea turtles come ashore to lay eggs. Slowing down and driving carefully near beaches helps them.
quests.funFact: Sea turtles lay eggs on beaches along parts of India's coast.

quests.instruction: In some seas, ships slow down to avoid hitting which giant animals?
quests.hint: They are the largest animals in the ocean.
quests.explanation: Whales can be hurt by fast ships. Slowing down gives both ships and whales time to avoid each other.
quests.funFact: Some ships change their routes during whale migration seasons.

quests.instruction: Which driving style saves fuel and reduces fumes?
quests.hint: Gentle is better.
quests.explanation: Smooth driving uses less fuel because the engine does not have to work as hard. Sudden speeding and braking waste energy.
quests.funFact: Planning ahead helps drivers brake less.

quests.instruction: A car waits at a long railway crossing with its engine running. What saves fuel and reduces fumes?
quests.hint: Turn it off while stopped for a long time.
quests.explanation: An engine that is running while the car is not moving burns fuel for no reason. Switching it off during long waits helps.
quests.funFact: Some modern cars switch their engines off automatically when stopped.

quests.instruction: Carrying heavy things you do not need makes a car use more fuel. What could you take out?
quests.hint: Think about extra weight.
quests.explanation: A heavier car needs more energy to move. Taking out unneeded bags and roof boxes can save fuel.
quests.funFact: Roof boxes also create wind resistance, which uses even more fuel.

quests.instruction: Old vehicles contain metal that can be melted and used again. What is this called?
quests.hint: Three arrows chase each other.
quests.explanation: Recycling means turning used materials into new ones. Much of a car can be recycled.
quests.funFact: Steel is one of the most recycled materials in the world.

quests.instruction: Old tyres can be shredded and made into soft surfaces for which place?
quests.hint: Children love it.
quests.explanation: Rubber from old tyres can be used for soft surfaces that protect children when they fall. It keeps tyres out of rubbish heaps.
quests.funFact: Recycled rubber is also used in running tracks and road surfaces.

quests.instruction: Which picture shows fixing something instead of throwing it away?
quests.hint: Mechanics use it for bicycles and cars.
quests.explanation: Fixing things keeps them working longer, so fewer new ones need to be made.
quests.funFact: Many towns have repair cafes where volunteers help fix bikes and other items.

quests.instruction: For a 400-kilometre trip between two cities with a good railway, which usually makes less pollution per person?
quests.hint: Its wheels roll on rails and it often uses electricity.
quests.explanation: Electric trains make less pollution per passenger than planes on routes like this. Trains also carry many people at once.
quests.funFact: Some countries have reduced short flights where fast trains are available.

quests.instruction: Which cleaner type of transport glides over traffic using electricity?
quests.hint: It hangs from cables.
quests.explanation: City cable cars run on electricity and travel above jammed streets, so they make little pollution where they run.
quests.funFact: Some cities use cable cars as part of their public transport.

quests.instruction: A hydrogen-powered bus gives out only one thing from its exhaust pipe. What is it?
quests.hint: It is the same thing that falls as rain.
quests.explanation: Hydrogen vehicles combine hydrogen with oxygen to make electricity, and only water is left over. They make no fumes.
quests.funFact: Hydrogen buses are being tested or used in several cities.

quests.instruction: A city adds more bus lanes, bike lanes, and trams. What is it trying to reduce?
quests.hint: It wants people to leave this at home more often.
quests.explanation: Planners aim to make walking, cycling, and public transport easy so fewer people need private cars for every trip.
quests.funFact: Cities with good alternatives often see lower car use.

quests.instruction: Some buses run on biogas made from food waste and plants. Which picture suggests where this fuel comes from?
quests.hint: It grows.
quests.explanation: Biogas is made when plant and food waste break down. It is renewable because new waste is made all the time.
quests.funFact: Biogas is also produced at farms and sewage plants.

quests.instruction: Ships in port can plug into the shore's electricity instead of running their engines. Which symbol shows the connection?
quests.hint: Think of how you charge a phone.
quests.explanation: Shore power means a ship does not need to burn fuel while waiting in port. That cuts fumes and noise near towns.
quests.funFact: Several big ports now offer plug-in power for ships.

quests.instruction: Choices like walking, cycling, sharing rides, and using public transport help keep which place healthy?
quests.hint: It is the planet we all share.
quests.explanation: Many small choices add up. Cleaner travel means cleaner air, less noise, and a more comfortable planet.
quests.funFact: People around the world are working on cleaner ways to travel.

quests.instruction: Combining several errands into one trip saves fuel. Which tool helps plan the best route?
quests.hint: It shows streets and shortcuts.
quests.explanation: Planning one efficient route means fewer, shorter journeys. That saves time, fuel, and money.
quests.funFact: Many people use apps to find the quickest or least busy route.

quests.instruction: A shop is only a ten-minute walk from home. What is the cleanest, healthiest way to go?
quests.hint: Use your own feet.
quests.explanation: Walking makes no pollution and gives exercise. For short trips, it is often the best choice.
quests.funFact: Walking regularly helps keep your heart and bones strong.
